title: Zero input validation on POST /api/analyze — no type checks, no address format, no length limit
evidence: body: AnalyzeRequest = await req.json() with zero runtime validation. Loop iterates body.addresses with no length cap (client-side max 5, server unlimited). No address format regex check (0x for EVM, base58 for Solana). No chain validation. Only limit is tokens.slice(0,20) for token scans. TypeScript types erased at runtime — no Zod/schema validation.
rationale: Unlimited addresses can be submitted server-side (client max-5 is bypassable via direct API call). Malformed addresses reach OnchainOS execSync (command injection vector, also flagged by P01:1.4). In demo mode, input is effectively ignored (cacheExists short-circuits), but the code path exists and is reachable if cache files are removed.
fix_guidance: Add Zod schema validation: max 5 addresses, regex patterns for EVM (0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}) and Solana (base58), chain whitelist. Or cap address count server-side. E2 because needs schema + validation logic.

title: Error responses leak internal error.message to client
evidence: All 4 API routes use the same error pattern: catch (error: any) { return NextResponse.json({ error: error.message }, { status: 500 }) }. This exposes internal error messages to the client — potential information leakage (file paths, OnchainOS command failures, cache file paths). cache.ts:9 also emits file paths: 'Cache file not found: ${filename}'.
rationale: In demo mode, errors are unlikely (cache always exists). But if an error occurs, the client sees internal file paths and error details. In production, this could expose server structure to attackers.
fix_guidance: Use generic error message in production: 'Internal server error'. Log full error details server-side only. Add NODE_ENV check: dev returns full error, production returns generic.

title: All 4 endpoints completely unauthenticated — intentional for demo
evidence: No authentication check on any endpoint. No middleware, no API key validation, no CORS origin check, no Authorization header parsing. All data is pre-cached mock data — no real user data exposed. The demo is designed to be publicly accessible.
rationale: Intentional for a hackathon demo — judges need to see the product without registering. All data is mock. Severity P2 because this is by design and no real data is at risk.
fix_guidance: Document that endpoints are intentionally open for evaluation. Add API key validation for production. For now: no action needed.

title: No CORS misconfiguration — same-origin by default is safe
evidence: next.config.ts has default Next.js config — no headers(), no CORS config. This means same-origin policy applies by default. Client fetch calls in page.tsx use relative URLs (/api/analyze etc.) — same-origin, no CORS needed. No Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is emitted. Safe by default for a single-origin app.
rationale: Same-origin policy is the secure default. Alter Ego is a single-origin Next.js app — the API routes are only called from the same origin. Adding CORS headers would WIDEN the attack surface, not narrow it.
fix_guidance: No action needed. If cross-origin API access is ever needed, add explicit CORS config with specific origins (not wildcard).

title: Next.js default error pages may expose framework version and stack traces in dev mode
evidence: All 4 routes catch errors and return error.message in JSON. In development mode (NODE_ENV=development), Next.js may also render full error overlays with stack traces. In production (Vercel deploy), error details are suppressed by Next.js defaults. No custom error page exists.
rationale: Development mode leaks framework internals — expected for dev, would be an issue if deployed in dev mode. Vercel production deploy auto-sets NODE_ENV=production, which suppresses Next.js error details.
fix_guidance: Verify Vercel deploys with NODE_ENV=production (should be default). Add a custom error.tsx page for graceful error handling. Strip error.message from production error responses.
